fr.elements: Open Green Space; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Install a turnaround area or widen the existing access drive near the detached structure to allow emergency vehicles to reverse direction without backing the full length of the drive.
• Keep the access drive surface clear of parked vehicles and equipment so emergency vehicles can reach the detached structure without obstruction.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the access drive to maintain overhead and lateral clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain a clear line of sight from the road to the structures.
• Keep a gate or barrier at the single access point unlocked or equipped with a Knox-style lock box so responders can enter without delay.
• Thin dense vegetation surrounding the detached structure to allow responders to move around all sides of the building on foot.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Grass Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetated Drainage; Single Access Route; Woody Debris; Mixed Vegetation; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Clear dead branches, fallen limbs, and woody debris from the ground around the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin scattered trees near the house so their branches do not touch or hang over the roof or walls.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the house.
• Separate shrubs and small trees growing near the house so there are visible gaps between them rather than a continuous line of plants leading to the structure.
• Mow or cut down dry grass growing close to the house, especially on the sides facing open terrain.
• Remove or cut back vegetation growing along the drainage channel where it runs closest to structures or the driveway.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove woody debris and dead plant material that has collected along the sides of the driveway.
• Thin mixed shrubs and small trees along the single access route so visibility is open and the road edge is clear.
• Cut back ground vegetation growing between the drainage area and any structures to reduce the connection between the two.
• Keep mowed or cleared areas around outbuildings, not just the main house, to reduce the chance of fire spreading between structures.
